gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-habibi: Habibi has a traditional, editorial voice, with a clear channel leading into each round letter. Habibi sits under Bruno Ace SC, whose wide-spread letters keep one constant stroke and never thin out, so a long page reads like a classic serif with a bold banner.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-inika: Expressive and distinctive, Bruno Ace SC spreads its letters out like beads on a thread. Inika follows with a text serif's old-fashioned manner, a visible gap in each s, giving the paragraph a soft hum beneath the heading.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-labrada: Bruno Ace SC draws tubular, wire-like letters spaced out like beads on a long thread. And Labrada, a dignified, bookish serif with wide openings on its small letters, gives that stylized heading something warmer to rest on.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-laila: Laila reads editorial and traditional, with generous space between curve ends and stems. Make Bruno Ace SC small and its sparkle-free, constant-weight letters lose their presence, while a large Laila would drift from the classic serif look it holds in text.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-montaga: Spaced-out and a bit futuristic, Bruno Ace SC opens its apertures wide and never thins a stroke into calligraphy. Montaga, a bookish serif, adds curves that lift off before the loop closes.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-new-tegomin: Wide, open and unshaded, Bruno Ace SC keeps its horizontals as heavy as its verticals, and that gives headings real presence. But New Tegomin, a dignified serif with a c like a wide-open ring, is the one built for traditional text.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-podkova: Podkova brings a bookish, traditional serif with a broad, welcoming c, set against Bruno Ace SC, whose strokes look identical whether they run up or sideways. The strongest quality here is that sharp split between the two.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-rhodium-libre: Wide, geometric and unhurried, Bruno Ace SC frames its counters with same-width strokes and open apertures. Rhodium Libre answers with a serif whose brush ends lift away before each curve closes.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-rokkitt: Rokkitt has a c as open as a bent paperclip. Next to Bruno Ace SC, which draws a single-width stroke in every glyph, its bookish text serif shows the strongest quality of the pair: two very different kinds of traditional and expressive.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-sanchez: Flat and stencil-cut, Bruno Ace SC holds every stroke to a single weight. Sanchez, a dignified serif with a c opened like a pair of calipers, brings a bookish texture underneath that the heading leaves out.
